audit_result.proof_trace: The proof fails immediately: `deleteMember` only executes `UPDATE members SET deleted_at = now()` and never touches `member_team_relations`, so the DB-layer post-condition `!exists(member_team_relations, m.id)` is never enforced. Current safety relies entirely on all consumers joining through `members WHERE deleted_at IS NULL` — a fragile application-level invariant with no DB-layer guarantee. Any new query against `member_team_relations` that omits the active-member filter would silently expose stale team affiliations of soft-deleted members.
audit_result.attack_scenario: An admin soft-deletes a member; the member's rows persist in `member_team_relations`. A future feature or a direct DB query (e.g., a reporting endpoint, analytics query, or a new page component) that reads `member_team_relations` without filtering through the `deleted_at IS NULL` member check would include the deleted member in team rosters, disclosing their historical team membership and inflating team member counts.

PROP-stem-system-post-002.text: After member soft-delete, all team assignments for that member must be removed.
